metadata.title: Household Finance Brokerage Platform Data Assets
metadata.description: Catalog of the household, identity and consent, consumer comparison and engagement, mortgage brokerage, insurance, energy and telecom brokerage, network and partner operations, and compliance, audit and analytics data assets that power the Peasy phygital brokerage model (hypotheek.winkel, Verzekeringen.be, Aanbieders.be) across about 70 offices, more than 50 partners and more than 50,000 contracts per year, with GDPR classification and national register number handling, health data for outstanding-balance insurance, EAN meter data, FSMA record-keeping for credit and insurance intermediation under Book VII of the Code of Economic Law and the IDD, Central Individual Credit Register consultation, BIPT Easy Switch, EU and Belgian data residency with controlled remote access from the Oujda care centre, backing stores and team ownership.

rootGroups.name: Household, Identity and Consent Data
rootGroups.description: The household record, logins, consents and the contract vault that turn a single mortgage or switch into a monitored household relationship across the three Peasy brands.

subGroups.name: Accounts, Identity and Consent
subGroups.description: Customer accounts, user identities for households, experts, advisors and partners, and the effective-dated consents that authorise every comparison, register consultation and switch.

assets.name: Customer Account
assets.description: One household relationship with Peasy across peasy.be, hypotheek.winkel, Verzekeringen.be and Aanbieders.be: the account holder and partner names, postal address and postcode, e-mail, mobile number, preferred language (NL or FR), household composition, the brand and channel through which the household first arrived, the assigned office or care team, and links to leads, appointments, credit files, policies and switches. Created when a visitor saves a simulation, books an appointment or requests a comparison, and mastered in the Household Contract Vault and Customer Account (cvlt), with the Multi-brand Site Shell (brnd) and care ticketing reading it on every contact.
assets.businessMeaning: The single household record that the three brands, the office network and the care centres all hang from: if it is wrong, the wrong expert calls the wrong family about the wrong contract.
assets.accessScope: the household for its own account; the assigned expert and office for their appointments and files; care advisors in Hasselt and Oujda for open tickets; customer engagement and compliance staff for lifecycle changes; never visible to other households, franchisees outside the assigned office or partners

interfaces.name: customer-account api
interfaces.description: Account creation, household profile, language and contact preferences, brand and channel attribution, office and care-team assignment and linked-object lookup API used by the site shell, the contract vault, the expert workbench, the care desk and lead routing.

interfaces.name: customer account events
interfaces.description: Household created, merged across brands, contact details changed, office assigned, care team assigned and account closed events consumed by the contract vault, cross-sell, ticketing, analytics and the audit trail.

governance.retention: kept while the household has an active brokered contract or open file and 10 years after the last credit or insurance intermediation act, because FSMA and Book VII record-keeping tie the advice to an identified client; accounts with only simulations or unconverted leads deleted after 3 years of inactivity; marketing preferences withdrawn immediately on request
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to the Peasy brands and the assigned franchised office; identification data passed to a bank or insurer only inside a submitted file, quote or switch order; never sold, never shared between partners, and accessed from the Oujda care centre only through controlled remote sessions on EU-hosted systems

assets.name: User Identity
assets.description: A login to a Peasy customer account, the expert workbench, the customer-care desk, the franchise back office, the academy or the partner portal: e-mail address, password hash, itsme or two-factor enrolment, device registrations, the roles the person holds (household member, hypotheek.expert, franchisee, care advisor, academy trainee, partner user, head-office administrator), the offices, brands or partner scopes the person may open, session and refresh tokens, invitation status and last sign-in. Managed by Identity, Consent and Access Control (iden) and checked on every screen and API call across the platform.
assets.businessMeaning: The gate to 70 offices worth of credit files and 50,000 contracts a year: correct scopes are what keep an expert inside their own office and a partner inside their own products.
assets.accessScope: the user for their own profile and devices; platform administrators for role and scope management; franchisees for the experts of their own office; network development for onboarding and offboarding experts; credentials and tokens never readable by anyone

interfaces.name: identity api
interfaces.description: Authentication, itsme and two-factor enrolment, session and refresh tokens, device registration, role and office, brand or partner scope authorisation checks, invitation and password-reset API used by every consumer site, workbench, back-office and partner module.

interfaces.name: identity events
interfaces.description: User invited, activated, role granted or revoked, office scope changed, suspicious sign-in, remote-access session opened and account deactivated events consumed by the audit trail, security monitoring, franchise management and the academy.

governance.retention: kept while the user is active and 2 years after deactivation so audit entries can still be attributed; expert and care-advisor identities kept 10 years in reduced form because FSMA-relevant advice must remain attributable to a registered person; sign-in logs kept 12 months; device registrations deleted when the user removes the device
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Peasy; itsme assertions exchanged with the identity provider for verification only; never shared with banks, insurers or other partners; an Oujda care advisor's identity carries a remote-access scope that is logged on every session

assets.name: Consent Record
assets.description: An effective-dated record of what a household or user agreed to and when: privacy statement version, cookie and analytics consent per brand site, marketing consent per channel (e-mail, SMS, phone), the mandate to compare and switch on the household's behalf, permission to consult the Central Individual Credit Register and to share the file with a chosen bank, explicit consent for health questions in outstanding-balance insurance, and withdrawal events. Written by Identity, Consent and Access Control (iden) from the sites, the workbench and the care desk, and consulted before any comparison, submission, alert or campaign touches the household.
assets.businessMeaning: The legal basis for every referral fee: a switch executed or a file shared without the matching consent is a complaint, an FSMA finding and a partner dispute waiting to happen.
assets.accessScope: the household for its own consents; experts and care advisors see the current state for the households they serve; compliance and risk for audits and data-subject requests; the platform team for registry maintenance; never editable outside the consent flows

interfaces.name: consent api
interfaces.description: Consent capture, current-state lookup per purpose and brand, mandate and register-consultation checks, withdrawal and proof-of-consent export API used by the site shell, comparison modules, the workbench, switch execution, monitoring alerts and campaigns.

interfaces.name: consent events
interfaces.description: Consent given, renewed, withdrawn and mandate signed events consumed by the contract vault, savings alerts, cross-sell, analytics tagging and the audit trail.

governance.retention: kept for the life of the relationship and 10 years after the last act it authorised, so a consultation of the credit register or a shared file can be matched to the consent that allowed it; withdrawn consents kept as proof of withdrawal for the same period; cookie consents expire and are re-asked after 13 months
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Peasy; the existence of a mandate or register consent is shown to a bank or insurer inside the submitted file only; never used for a purpose other than the one recorded; marketing consent never transferred between brands without an explicit cross-brand opt-in

subGroups.name: Household Relationship and Monitoring
subGroups.description: Brokered contracts stored per household, the savings alerts computed on them and the consolidated customer 360 profile used for cross-sell.

assets.name: Household Contract
assets.description: One brokered contract stored in a household's vault: the contract type (mortgage loan, car, fire, funeral or outstanding-balance policy, electricity, gas, internet and TV pack, mobile plan), the partner it was concluded with, the reference and start date, tariff or premium and monthly cost, the key parameters used for re-comparison (loan amount and rate, insured vehicle or dwelling, EAN meter numbers and annual consumption, telecom pack and data volume), renewal or fixed-term end date, documents on file and the Peasy contact who arranged it. Mastered in the Household Contract Vault and Customer Account (cvlt) and fed by closing, policy binding and switch execution.
assets.businessMeaning: The household relationship made concrete: the more contracts in the vault, the more often Peasy can prove it is cheaper elsewhere and earn the next referral fee.
assets.accessScope: the household for its own vault; the assigned expert and care advisors for households they serve; customer engagement for monitoring rules; the partner sees only its own contract through reconciliation; renewal dates and consumption readable by the alert engine without identification

interfaces.name: household-contract api
interfaces.description: Vault listing, contract detail, parameter update, document attachment, renewal-date and re-comparison-parameter lookup API used by the customer account, monitoring, cross-sell, the care desk and the expert workbench.

interfaces.name: household contract events
interfaces.description: Contract added to vault, parameters updated, renewal approaching, contract replaced by a switch and contract ended events consumed by monitoring, savings alerts, the customer 360 profile, commission reconciliation and analytics.

governance.retention: kept while the contract is active and 10 years after it ends or is replaced, matching the intermediation record-keeping of the credit file or policy it belongs to; EAN numbers and consumption figures pruned to the last two years once the energy contract has ended; deleted earlier on a valid erasure request when no intermediation obligation remains
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Peasy; a contract's parameters go to a new partner only inside a switch order or quote the household approved; consumption and premium history never shared with the losing partner; aggregated per-partner volumes only in reconciliation

assets.name: Savings Alert
assets.description: A monitoring outcome computed for one household contract: the trigger (renewal window, fixed-term end, tariff change at the current partner, a cheaper partner tariff in the comparison engine, a rate movement relevant to a refinancing case, or a budget barometer gap), the estimated annual saving in euro, the recommended partner product and the comparison snapshot behind it, the channel and moment chosen to contact the household, the advisor who follows it up, and the outcome (accepted, declined, snoozed, expired). Produced by Renewal Monitoring and Savings Alerts (mntr) and handed to customer care or the expert who owns the relationship.
assets.businessMeaning: The promise that Peasy keeps watching: an alert the household accepts is a new switch, a new referral fee and the reason the vault stays full.
assets.accessScope: the household for its own alerts; care advisors and the assigned expert for the alerts they follow up; customer engagement and comparison-modules teams for rule tuning on pseudonymised data; partners never see which of their customers was alerted

interfaces.name: savings-alert api
interfaces.description: Alert listing per household and per advisor queue, alert detail with comparison snapshot, snooze, decline and accept API used by the customer account, the care desk, cross-sell and the expert workbench.

interfaces.name: savings alert events
interfaces.description: Alert generated, sent, opened, accepted, declined, snoozed and expired events consumed by ticketing, the customer 360 profile, campaign suppression and analytics.

governance.retention: alerts and their outcomes kept 3 years so acceptance rates and suppression rules can be tuned and a household is not alerted twice for the same contract; the comparison snapshot behind an accepted alert kept with the resulting contract for 10 years; expired alerts pseudonymised after 13 months
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Peasy; the household sees its own alerts; the winning partner receives only the resulting quote or switch order; never shared with the current partner or used to negotiate on the household's behalf without a mandate

assets.name: Customer 360 Profile
assets.description: The consolidated view of a household across the three brands: contracts in the vault by category, open files and tickets, the last simulation and comparison, life-stage signals (first home, renovation obligation, second home, new child, moving), next-best-offer scores for insurance, energy, telecom and refinancing, estimated household saving potential against the budget barometer, contact preferences and suppression flags, and the relationship owner. Recomputed by Customer 360 and Cross-sell Engine (crmx) from the vault, leads and care tickets, and shown to experts and care advisors before any conversation.
assets.businessMeaning: Turns one mortgage into a household relationship: the profile tells the advisor which contract to raise next and stops three brands from calling the same family in one week.
assets.accessScope: the assigned expert and care advisors for households they serve; customer engagement for scoring rules on pseudonymised data; compliance for a data-subject access report; the household sees the underlying contracts and consents but not the scores; never visible to partners

interfaces.name: customer-360 api
interfaces.description: Household overview, next-best-offer scores, saving potential, suppression flags and relationship-owner lookup API used by the care desk, the expert workbench, monitoring, campaigns and the customer account.

interfaces.name: customer 360 events
interfaces.description: Profile recomputed, next-best-offer changed, suppression flag set and relationship owner changed events consumed by lead routing, savings alerts, campaigns and analytics.

governance.retention: recomputed continuously and kept while the household has an active contract or open file; scores and signals expire after 12 months without refresh; deleted with the customer account, and the derivation logic documented so a data-subject request can explain any score
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Peasy; scores never disclosed to partners, franchisees outside the relationship or the household as a credit or risk judgement; used only to prioritise contacts the household consented to

rootGroups.name: Consumer Comparison and Engagement Data
rootGroups.description: What the consumer sites capture before an expert or advisor is involved: simulations, certificates, uploaded proposals, budget profiles, comparison requests, partner tariffs, leads, appointments and callbacks.

subGroups.name: Simulations, Certificates and Content
subGroups.description: Mortgage simulator runs, feasibility certificates, uploaded proposals for review, budget barometer profiles and the published content of the brand sites.

assets.name: Simulation Result
assets.description: The input and output of one run of a hypotheek.winkel simulator on peasy.be or hypotheekwinkel.be: how much can I borrow, monthly repayment, rate check, financial plan, notary costs or amortisation table; household net income and existing loans, own funds and savings, project type (first home, next home, second home, new build, renovation loan, self-employed), property price, region and EPC label for the renovation obligation, the resulting maximum loan, monthly instalment, notary and registration cost estimate, and whether the visitor saved the result, requested a certificate or booked an appointment. Produced by the Borrowing Capacity and Monthly Repayment Simulator (simb) and reused by feasibility and notary calculators.
assets.businessMeaning: The top of the mortgage funnel: every saved simulation is a household with a project, and its numbers pre-fill the expert's first appointment.
assets.accessScope: the visitor or household for its own simulations; the assigned expert once an appointment is booked; the consumer platform team for calculator diagnostics on pseudonymised data; anonymous simulations readable by analytics only in aggregate

interfaces.name: simulation api
interfaces.description: Run, save, retrieve and pre-fill API for borrowing capacity, monthly repayment, rate, financial plan, notary cost and amortisation simulations used by the consumer sites, the feasibility certificate, the notary calculator, appointment booking and the expert workbench.

interfaces.name: simulation events
interfaces.description: Simulation completed, saved, converted to certificate request and converted to appointment events consumed by lead routing, the customer 360 profile and analytics.

governance.retention: anonymous simulations pseudonymised after 30 days and kept only in aggregate; simulations linked to an account kept 3 years so the expert can see the household's earlier projects; simulations that became a credit file kept with that file for 10 years
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Peasy; simulation figures reach a bank only after the expert has turned them into a credit file; never shared with real-estate agents or sellers except through a certificate the household requested

assets.name: Feasibility Certificate
assets.description: The haalbaarheidscertificaat a buyer shows to a seller or estate agent: the household's borrowing capacity checked by a hypotheek.expert against the daily conditions of 25 banks on the basis of salary and savings, the maximum purchase price and loan amount it supports, the assumptions used (own funds, term, renovation budget required for a low-EPC home), the issuing expert and office, the FSMA registration reference, issue date and validity window, a verification code and the PDF as delivered in NL or FR. Issued by Feasibility Check and Certificate (feas) after a simulation and, where needed, a short appointment.
assets.businessMeaning: Peasy's proof of buying power in a competitive housing market: it wins the seller's trust for the buyer and binds the buyer to the office that issued it.
assets.accessScope: the household for its own certificate and the verification page it chooses to share; the issuing expert and office; compliance for sampling; a seller or agent sees only what the verification code exposes (validity and supported price), never income or savings

interfaces.name: feasibility-certificate api
interfaces.description: Certificate request, expert check, issuance, verification-code lookup and re-issue API used by the consumer sites, the expert workbench, appointment booking and the customer account.

interfaces.name: feasibility certificate events
interfaces.description: Certificate requested, checked, issued, verified by a third party, expired and converted to a credit file events consumed by lead routing, production dashboards, the customer 360 profile and analytics.

interfaces.name: certificate pdf
interfaces.description: Bilingual PDF of the certificate delivered to the household and stored in the document store, carrying the verification code and issuing office.

governance.retention: kept 10 years from issue as part of the advice record of the intermediary, because it states a borrowing capacity checked by a registered expert; the verification page stops answering after the validity window; the PDF removed from the household account on request once the file is closed
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with a seller or estate agent only by the household, through the PDF or verification code; the underlying income and savings never leave Peasy; banks receive the certificate only inside the credit file

assets.name: Uploaded Proposal
assets.description: A mortgage or insurance proposal a household received elsewhere and uploaded for a free expert review: the document itself (bank offer, broker comparison, insurer quote), the extracted key terms (lender or insurer, amount, term, rate type and rate, monthly instalment, fees, cover and premium), the household's contact details and question, the expert or care advisor assigned, the counter-comparison prepared against the daily bank conditions or the 11 insurers, and the verdict returned to the household with the recommended next step. Captured by Upload-Your-Proposal Intake (upld) and handed to the comparison engine and lead routing.
assets.businessMeaning: The cheapest refinancing lead Peasy has: a household that already has an offer, wants it beaten and gets a verdict from an expert within days.
assets.accessScope: the household for its own upload and verdict; the assigned expert or care advisor; the consumer platform team for extraction diagnostics on samples the household consented to; never visible to the bank or insurer whose proposal is being reviewed

interfaces.name: uploaded-proposal api
interfaces.description: Upload, extracted-terms review, assignment, counter-comparison attachment and verdict delivery API used by the consumer sites, lead routing, the expert workbench and the care desk.

interfaces.name: uploaded proposal events
interfaces.description: Proposal uploaded, terms extracted, assigned, verdict sent and converted to a refinancing case or quote events consumed by lead routing, production dashboards, the customer 360 profile and analytics.

interfaces.name: proposal document
interfaces.description: The original PDF or image the household uploaded, encrypted at rest and linked to the verdict.

governance.retention: kept 2 years when the review leads nowhere, so a returning household does not upload twice; kept 10 years with the advice record when the review becomes a refinancing case or a bound policy; the original document deleted on request as soon as the verdict has been delivered
governance.sharingPolicy: never shown to the competing bank or insurer; the counter-proposal goes to a new bank only inside a credit file the household chose to submit; internal to the assigned expert or care advisor and compliance sampling

assets.name: Budget Profile
assets.description: A household's entry in the Peasy budget barometer: household size and type, region, dwelling type and ownership, the monthly amounts it declares for mortgage or rent, car, fire, funeral and outstanding-balance insurance, electricity, gas, internet and TV, mobile and other fixed costs, the Belgian reference averages applied, the resulting overpayment gaps per category, the categories the household chose to compare next, and links to the resulting comparison requests. Created by the Budget Barometer (bgtb) and refreshed when a switch or alert changes a monthly amount.
assets.businessMeaning: Shows a family where it overpays versus the Belgian average and turns the answer into a queue of comparisons, which is how the barometer feeds every comparison module.
assets.accessScope: the household for its own profile; care advisors and the assigned expert for households they serve; the consumer platform team for reference-average maintenance and diagnostics on pseudonymised data; never visible to partners

interfaces.name: budget-profile api
interfaces.description: Barometer input, reference-average lookup, gap computation, category selection and refresh API used by the consumer sites, the comparison modules, monitoring, cross-sell and the customer account.

interfaces.name: budget profile events
interfaces.description: Profile created, gaps computed, category selected for comparison and profile refreshed after a switch events consumed by comparison requests, savings alerts, the customer 360 profile and analytics.

governance.retention: anonymous barometer runs pseudonymised after 30 days; profiles linked to an account kept 3 years and refreshed as contracts change; deleted with the customer account; reference averages kept indefinitely as non-personal data
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Peasy; declared amounts never shared with partners; only aggregated overpayment statistics per category and region used in content and campaigns

assets.name: Content Article
assets.description: A published piece of the peasy.be, hypotheekwinkel.be, verzekeringen.be or aanbieders.be sites: blog article, FAQ entry, guide (notary costs, renovation obligation, digital meter, Easy Switch), insurer or partner page, office landing page, simulator explanation or legal notice; NL and FR versions, brand and language routing, author and review date, the compliance approval for anything that mentions rates, premiums or savings claims, SEO metadata, related simulators and comparison modules, and publication state. Managed in Content, Blog and FAQ Pages (cont) and rendered by the site shell; no household data inside.
assets.businessMeaning: The organic front door of three brands: content ranks the simulators and comparison modules on Google and must never promise a rate or saving compliance has not approved.
assets.accessScope: the public reads published pages; marketing and the consumer platform team author and publish; compliance approves pages carrying rates, premiums or savings claims; franchisees may propose edits to their own office page

interfaces.name: content api
interfaces.description: Page and article retrieval per brand and language, FAQ search, office page lookup, related-tool links and publication workflow API used by the site shell, the knowledge base and the office locator.

interfaces.name: content events
interfaces.description: Article drafted, compliance-approved, published, updated and unpublished events consumed by the site shell, search indexing and analytics.

governance.retention: published versions kept 10 years so any rate, premium or savings claim shown to the public can be reproduced for FSMA or the Economic Inspectorate; drafts deleted 12 months after abandonment
governance.sharingPolicy: public once published; partner pages reviewed with the partner where the agreement requires it; no personal data, so no restriction on sharing beyond copyright

subGroups.name: Comparison Requests and Partner Tariffs
subGroups.description: Insurance, energy and telecom comparison runs and the effective-dated partner tariffs they are computed from.

assets.name: Comparison Request
assets.description: One comparison run on Verzekeringen.be, Aanbieders.be or by a care advisor: the category (car, fire, funeral, outstanding-balance or other insurance; electricity and gas; internet, TV and mobile), the household inputs (vehicle and driver history, dwelling and contents, insured amount and health-question flags for outstanding-balance cover, postcode, meter type, digital meter, solar panels and annual consumption, current pack and data usage), the tariff versions compared, the ranked results with estimated annual saving, the option the household selected, the channel (self-service, phone, chat) and the resulting quote or switch order. Mastered per category by the insurance (insc), energy (enrg) and telecom (tlcm) comparison modules, with insc carrying the shared model, and reused by quote and bind, switch execution and monitoring.
assets.businessMeaning: The unit of work of the comparison business: a request that ends in a selected option is a quote or switch, a referral fee and a contract in the vault.
assets.accessScope: the household for its own requests; care advisors for requests they handle; the comparison-modules team for engine diagnostics on pseudonymised data; health-question flags readable only by the insurance quote module; partners never see a request that did not select them

interfaces.name: comparison api
interfaces.description: Run, rank, save, resume and select API for insurance, energy and telecom comparisons used by the consumer sites, the care desk, the budget barometer, monitoring and switch execution.

interfaces.name: comparison events
interfaces.description: Comparison started, completed, option selected, abandoned and converted to quote or switch events consumed by lead routing, savings alerts, the customer 360 profile, partner reporting and analytics.

governance.retention: anonymous requests pseudonymised after 30 days; requests linked to an account kept 3 years so a household can resume or re-run them; the request behind a bound policy or executed switch kept 10 years with that contract; health-question answers deleted once the insurer has issued the policy unless the household asks Peasy to keep them for the next comparison
governance.sharingPolicy: the selected partner receives only the inputs needed to quote or switch; losing partners see aggregated win and loss statistics only; health answers passed to the insurer alone and never stored in the warehouse

assets.name: Partner Product Tariff
assets.description: One effective-dated version of a product from the more than 50 partners in the comparison engine: insurer product and cover options with premium formulas and underwriting rules for the 11 insurers on Verzekeringen.be, electricity and gas tariff cards per region, meter type and consumption band including the prosumer tariff and green-energy label, internet, TV and mobile packs with promotions and Easy Switch eligibility, the feed or file it came from, validation status and the commission scheme reference. Maintained by the Partner Product Catalogue and Tariff Feeds (pcat) and read by every comparison module.
assets.businessMeaning: The truth behind every saving Peasy promises: a wrong or stale tariff means a wrong recommendation, a partner dispute and a household that stops trusting the comparison.
assets.accessScope: the comparison-modules and partner-management teams maintain and validate; comparison modules, monitoring and the care desk read the current version; partners see and correct only their own products through the partner portal; commission scheme references hidden from advisors and households

interfaces.name: tariff api
interfaces.description: Effective-dated tariff and product lookup, premium and cost computation, eligibility rules, promotion and validation-status API used by the comparison modules, the budget barometer, monitoring, the care desk and the partner portal.

interfaces.name: tariff events
interfaces.description: Tariff version received, validated, published, corrected and withdrawn events consumed by the comparison modules, savings alerts, partner reporting and analytics.

interfaces.name: partner tariff feed
interfaces.description: Daily or event-driven tariff files and API pulls from insurers, energy suppliers and telecom operators, kept as received for feed accuracy disputes.

governance.retention: every version kept 10 years so a comparison shown to a household or a commission computed for a partner can be replayed; feed files kept 2 years for accuracy disputes; withdrawn products remain visible in historical comparisons only
governance.sharingPolicy: partner tariffs are confidential to Peasy and the partner concerned; never shown to competing partners in raw form; households see computed premiums and costs, not underwriting rules; aggregated feed-accuracy statistics shared with each partner

subGroups.name: Leads, Appointments and Callbacks
subGroups.description: The intent signals routed to the office network and the care centres and the meetings and callbacks they become.

assets.name: Lead
assets.description: A household with an intent Peasy can act on: source (simulator, feasibility request, upload, comparison, callback, chat, Google review click, partner referral or Meilleurtaux hand-over), brand and language, category (mortgage project type, refinancing, insurance, energy, telecom), contact details and postcode, qualification score and consent state, the office or care team it was routed to and why (proximity, capacity, expertise), the owner, response time, status (new, contacted, appointment booked, converted, lost) and the resulting appointment, file or comparison. Owned by Lead Routing and Distribution (lead) and created by every consumer entry point.
assets.businessMeaning: The commodity the franchise network lives on: a qualified lead routed to the nearest office in minutes is an appointment, and appointments are what franchisees pay the brand for.
assets.accessScope: the receiving office or care team and its owner; network development for routing rules and reallocation; franchisees for their own office's leads; partners referring a lead see only its status; never visible to other offices

interfaces.name: lead api
interfaces.description: Lead creation, qualification, routing decision, assignment, status and conversion-link API used by the simulators, upload intake, comparison modules, appointment booking, callback requests, the partner portal, the workbench and the care desk.

interfaces.name: lead events
interfaces.description: Lead created, qualified, routed, reassigned, contacted, converted and lost events consumed by production dashboards, the customer 360 profile, partner reconciliation and analytics.

governance.retention: unconverted leads kept 2 years and then deleted unless the household has an account; converted leads kept with the resulting file or contract for 10 years as the origin of the intermediation; routing decisions kept 3 years for franchise fairness disputes
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Peasy and the receiving franchised office; a referring partner learns only whether its lead converted; never sold or passed to another intermediary; Meilleurtaux hand-overs governed by the group's intra-group agreement

assets.name: Appointment
assets.description: A booked meeting between a household and a hypotheek.expert or care advisor: office (one of about 70) or video call, date and slot, the expert, the household's project or question, documents the household was asked to bring (payslips, tax assessment, compromis, EPC), preparation notes pulled from the simulation or lead, confirmation and reminder messages sent by e-mail and SMS, rescheduling history, attendance and outcome (file opened, certificate issued, follow-up planned, no-show). Created by Appointment Booking and Office Locator (appt) and consumed by the expert workbench and production dashboards.
assets.businessMeaning: Where the phygital model becomes a conversation: the appointment is the north-star unit for franchisees and the moment a lead becomes a file.
assets.accessScope: the household for its own appointments; the expert and office holding the slot; care advisors for rescheduling; franchisees for their office's calendar; network development for capacity reporting in aggregate

interfaces.name: appointment api
interfaces.description: Slot search per office and expert, booking, rescheduling, cancellation, preparation-note and outcome API used by the consumer sites, lead routing, the workbench, the care desk and the customer account.

interfaces.name: appointment events
interfaces.description: Appointment booked, confirmed, reminded, rescheduled, attended, no-show and outcome-recorded events consumed by lead status, production dashboards, the customer 360 profile and analytics.

governance.retention: kept 3 years for capacity planning and no-show analysis; appointments that opened a credit file kept with that file for 10 years; reminder message logs deleted after 12 months
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Peasy and the assigned office; calendar details never shared with partners; video-call links single-use and expiring

assets.name: Callback Request
assets.description: A request to be called back or a chat conversation started on any of the brand sites or by phone outside opening hours: name, phone number, preferred moment, language, brand and page of origin, the question as typed, category detection, the queue it was placed in (mortgage office, Hasselt or Oujda care centre), the advisor who picked it up, attempts and reach time, and the outcome (comparison run, appointment booked, ticket opened, unreachable). Captured by Callback and Chat Requests (cbck) and routed through the contact-centre platform.
assets.businessMeaning: The lowest-friction way into Peasy: a callback answered within the promised window is the first-contact resolution the care centres are measured on.
assets.accessScope: the advisor and queue handling the request; care-centre team leads for queue management; the customer engagement team for routing diagnostics; the requester sees the status of their own request

interfaces.name: callback api
interfaces.description: Request capture, queue placement, pick-up, attempt logging and outcome API used by the consumer sites, the care desk, lead routing and ticketing.

interfaces.name: callback events
interfaces.description: Callback requested, queued, picked up, reached, unreachable and closed events consumed by lead creation, ticketing, care-centre dashboards and analytics.

governance.retention: kept 12 months for service-level reporting and then deleted unless converted to a lead or ticket; chat transcripts kept 12 months; phone numbers of unreached requesters deleted after the last attempt window
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Peasy care centres and mortgage offices; never shared with partners; Oujda advisors reach the queue through controlled remote sessions on EU-hosted systems

rootGroups.name: Mortgage Brokerage Data
rootGroups.description: What the hypotheek.winkel expert workbench holds: the daily conditions of 25 banks, proposals and advice records, credit files and their documents, bank submissions, closing milestones and refinancing cases.

subGroups.name: Bank Conditions and Advice
subGroups.description: Daily bank rate sheets, the multi-bank proposals computed from them and the FSMA-required advice and suitability records.

assets.name: Bank Rate Sheet
assets.description: The daily conditions of one of the 25 banks hypotheek.winkel compares: effective date, rate grids per term, fixed and variable formulas and revision caps, quotity and debt-ratio limits, discounts tied to fire and outstanding-balance insurance or a current account, file and estimate fees, energy-efficient and renovation loan conditions, acceptance rules for self-employed borrowers, promotional windows, the negotiated broker margin and the source (bank feed, e-mail circular, portal download) with validation status. Loaded by the Daily Bank Rate and Conditions Feed (rate) each morning and frozen per version for every comparison.
assets.businessMeaning: The reason a household visits an expert instead of one bank: 25 rate sheets on one screen, refreshed daily, are the comparison advantage the whole brokerage rests on.
assets.accessScope: the mortgage workbench team loads and validates; experts and the comparison engine read the current version; head-office partner management sees negotiated margins; households see only the resulting proposals; never disclosed to other banks

interfaces.name: bank-rate-sheet api
interfaces.description: Effective-dated rate grid, condition and acceptance-rule lookup, validation-status and margin API used by the proposal comparison engine, the feasibility check, the simulators, refinancing cases and production reporting.

interfaces.name: bank rate sheet events
interfaces.description: Sheet received, validated, published, corrected and expired events consumed by the comparison engine, savings alerts for refinancing, partner reporting and analytics.

interfaces.name: bank conditions feed
interfaces.description: Daily rate files, circulars and portal exports from the 25 banks kept as received so any comparison can be traced to its source.

governance.retention: every version kept 10 years so the advice given on any day can be reconstructed for FSMA or a complaint; source files kept 5 years; promotional windows remain visible in historical comparisons only
governance.sharingPolicy: confidential between Peasy and each bank; a bank's conditions shown to households only as computed proposals; negotiated margins never shown to experts, franchisees or households; never shared with competing banks

assets.name: Mortgage Proposal
assets.description: The same-screen comparison an expert prepares for one project: the household's situation (income, own funds, existing loans, project type, property price, EPC and renovation budget), the candidate offers computed from up to 25 bank rate sheets with rate, term, monthly instalment, total cost of credit, required insurance and account conditions, the ranking and the expert's recommended total package with the reasons, any proposal received elsewhere used as benchmark, the version shown to the household, and the household's choice. Produced by the Multi-bank Proposal Comparison Engine (cmpr) and turned into the advice record and the credit file.
assets.businessMeaning: The independent recommendation that justifies the referral fee: the best total package across 25 banks, documented so the household and the FSMA can see why.
assets.accessScope: the household for proposals shown to it; the preparing expert and their office; compliance for sampling and complaints; the mortgage workbench team for engine diagnostics on pseudonymised data; the chosen bank sees only the file that follows, never the competing offers

interfaces.name: mortgage-proposal api
interfaces.description: Proposal computation from situation and project, ranking, recommendation drafting, version sharing with the household and choice-capture API used by the expert workbench, the advice record, refinancing cases and the credit file.

interfaces.name: mortgage proposal events
interfaces.description: Proposal computed, shared, revised, chosen and abandoned events consumed by the advice record, credit file creation, production dashboards, the customer 360 profile and analytics.

interfaces.name: proposal comparison pdf
interfaces.description: The one-page comparison and recommendation delivered to the household in NL or FR and archived with the advice record.

governance.retention: kept 10 years after the loan is concluded or the file is closed without a loan, as part of the intermediary's advice record under FSMA and Book VII record-keeping; the shared PDF removed from the household account on request once the loan is in the vault
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the household and the chosen bank only through the credit file; competing offers never disclosed to any bank; never used to negotiate with a bank without the household's mandate

assets.name: Advice Record
assets.description: The FSMA-required record of the credit or insurance advice given to a household: the demands and needs analysis, the information collected on income, commitments, savings and objectives, the knowledge and experience assessment, the products considered and the suitability reasoning, warnings given (variable rate, renovation obligation, cover exclusions) and, for outstanding-balance cover, the health-related elements of the demands-and-needs analysis, the advisor's FSMA registration reference, the household's acknowledgement and signature by e-signature or in the office, versions and the link to the proposal, credit file, quote or policy it concerns. Written in Advice Record and Suitability Assessment (advr) and reviewed through Compliance, Complaints and Audit Trail (cmpl).
assets.businessMeaning: The document the FSMA asks for first and the intermediary's defence in any complaint: without it the referral fee was earned on advice nobody can prove was suitable.
assets.accessScope: the household for its own records; the advising expert or advisor and their office; compliance and risk for review, sampling and complaint handling; never editable after signature, only versioned; the bank or insurer receives the parts the file requires

interfaces.name: advice-record api
interfaces.description: Demands-and-needs capture, suitability assessment, warning checklist, signature request and immutable-version retrieval API used by the expert workbench, insurance quote and binding, refinancing cases, the care desk and compliance review.

interfaces.name: advice record events
interfaces.description: Record drafted, completed, signed, versioned, sampled by compliance and attached to a complaint events consumed by the credit file, policy binding, compliance dashboards and the audit trail.

interfaces.name: signed advice record
interfaces.description: The signed PDF of the advice record delivered to the household and archived immutably in the document store.

governance.retention: kept 10 years after the end of the intermediation relationship for credit advice and at least 5 years for insurance advice, and longer while a complaint or dispute is open; never deleted on a household erasure request while the legal retention runs; then destroyed with the audit entry of the destruction kept
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Peasy and the assigned office; the relevant parts passed to the bank or insurer inside the file; disclosed to the FSMA, the Economic Inspectorate or an ombudsman on request; never shared with other partners or between offices

subGroups.name: Credit File and Closing
subGroups.description: The credit file, its evidence documents, submissions to banks, closing milestones through notary and insurance, and refinancing cases.

assets.name: Credit File
assets.description: The mortgage dossier an expert assembles for one project: borrowers with national register number, civil status and address, employment and income per borrower (payslips, tax assessments, accounts for the self-employed), existing credits and the Central Individual Credit Register consultation result, own funds and savings, the property (compromis, price, valuation, EPC, renovation budget), the chosen bank and product from the proposal, the document checklist with completeness status, conditions requested by the bank, and the file status from draft to submitted, approved, declined or withdrawn. Mastered in Credit File and Document Collection (cfil) and submitted through Bank Submission and Approval Tracking (bsub).
assets.businessMeaning: The expert's product: a first-time-complete file is what banks approve quickly, what the buyer needs before the compromis deadline and what the north-star metrics count.
assets.accessScope: the household for its own file; the assembling expert and office; head-office compliance for review; the chosen bank receives the submitted version; national register numbers masked outside the file and submission modules; never visible to other offices or partners

interfaces.name: credit-file api
interfaces.description: File creation from a proposal, borrower and property data capture, register-consultation logging, checklist and completeness scoring, bank-condition tracking and status API used by the expert workbench, bank submission, closing tracking, refinancing cases and production dashboards.

interfaces.name: credit file events
interfaces.description: File opened, document received, completeness reached, submitted, condition raised, approved, declined and withdrawn events consumed by bank submission, closing, production dashboards, the customer 360 profile, commission reconciliation and analytics.

governance.retention: kept 10 years after the loan is concluded (credit intermediation records under Book VII and FSMA) and 5 years after a declined or abandoned file; register consultation results kept only as long as Book VII allows; national register numbers removed at the end of retention with the destruction logged
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the chosen bank only, as the submitted file the household approved; never sent to more than one bank at a time without a mandate; disclosed to the FSMA or the Economic Inspectorate on request; never shared with insurers beyond the fields a linked policy needs

assets.name: Credit File Document
assets.description: One evidence document inside a credit file: identity card copy, payslips, tax assessment, employer statement, accounts of a self-employed borrower, savings and investment statements, existing loan tables, the signed compromis, the EPC certificate, valuation report, building quotes for a renovation loan, the feasibility certificate and the signed advice record; with document type, borrower it concerns, upload channel (customer account, e-mail, scanned in the office), extraction and validity checks, expert acceptance, the bank's acceptance or rejection reason, and versions. Stored by Credit File and Document Collection (cfil) in the encrypted document store.
assets.businessMeaning: Where files stall: a missing or rejected document is the most common reason approval takes days longer, so each document's status is tracked like a milestone.
assets.accessScope: the household uploads and sees its own documents; the assembling expert and office accept them; compliance for sampling; the chosen bank receives the accepted set inside the submission; never readable by other offices, care advisors or partners

interfaces.name: credit-file-document api
interfaces.description: Upload, classification, validity check, expert acceptance, bank rejection handling and versioned retrieval API used by the customer account, the expert workbench, bank submission and closing tracking.

interfaces.name: credit file document events
interfaces.description: Document requested, uploaded, classified, accepted, rejected by the bank and replaced events consumed by the credit file checklist, household reminders, production dashboards and the audit trail.

interfaces.name: evidence document
interfaces.description: The encrypted original (PDF or image) as uploaded or scanned, immutable once the file is submitted.

governance.retention: kept with the credit file for 10 years after the loan is concluded and 5 years after a declined or abandoned file; documents the household withdraws before submission deleted immediately; identity copies retained only as long as Book VII identification duties require
governance.sharingPolicy: transferred to the chosen bank inside the submission only; never forwarded to insurers, notaries or partners except the specific document a closing step requires and the household approved; downloads by staff logged in the audit trail

assets.name: Bank Submission
assets.description: One transmission of a credit file to a bank and everything that comes back: the bank and product, submission channel (bank broker portal, API, secure e-mail), package contents and checksum, submission timestamp and the expert who released it, acknowledgement, the bank's questions and additional conditions, missing-document requests, approval in principle, final approval with offer letter and conditions, decline reason, turnaround times per step, and the resubmission chain when a file is corrected or moved to another bank. Tracked by Bank Submission and Approval Tracking (bsub) through the Integration Gateway (intg).
assets.businessMeaning: The handshake with the partner that pays: submission data shows each bank how complete Peasy's files are and shows Peasy which bank approves fastest.
assets.accessScope: the releasing expert and office; the household for the status of its own file; the bank for its own submissions through its portal or API; the platform and integration team for transport diagnostics without payload content; partner management for turnaround reporting in aggregate

interfaces.name: bank-submission api
interfaces.description: Package assembly, release, acknowledgement and bank-response capture, condition and missing-document tracking, approval and decline recording and resubmission API used by the expert workbench, the integration gateway, closing tracking and production dashboards.

interfaces.name: bank submission events
interfaces.description: File submitted, acknowledged, questioned, approved in principle, approved, declined and resubmitted events consumed by closing tracking, production dashboards, commission reconciliation, partner reporting and analytics.

interfaces.name: submission package
interfaces.description: The file package as sent to the bank and the offer letter and conditions as received, kept as transmitted for dispute resolution.

governance.retention: kept 10 years with the credit file, because the submission proves what was sent to the bank and when; transport logs kept 2 years; packages for withdrawn files kept 5 years
governance.sharingPolicy: exchanged with the receiving bank only; the bank's decision never disclosed to another bank; turnaround statistics shared with each bank about its own files; disclosed to the FSMA on request

assets.name: Closing Milestone
assets.description: A step on the way from bank approval to keys in hand for one file: offer letter signed, outstanding-balance insurance accepted (including medical acceptance), fire insurance bound, notary appointed, deed date planned, funds requested, deed signed, disbursement confirmed, and follow-up tasks such as domiciliation and mortgage registration; each with due date, responsible party (household, expert, bank, insurer, notary), documents exchanged, blockers and the expert's follow-up notes. Tracked by Closing, Notary and Disbursement Tracking (clos), which also attaches the resulting policies to the household contract vault.
assets.businessMeaning: The last mile where a deal can still die: tracking notary and insurance steps is what keeps compromis deadlines and earns the commission that is only paid at deed.
assets.accessScope: the household for its own timeline; the following expert and office; care advisors binding the linked insurance; the platform team for e-signature diagnostics; notaries and banks see only the step that concerns them

interfaces.name: closing-milestone api
interfaces.description: Milestone plan creation from an approval, due-date and responsible-party tracking, blocker logging, deed-date and disbursement confirmation and vault hand-over API used by the expert workbench, insurance binding, the customer account and production dashboards.

interfaces.name: closing milestone events
interfaces.description: Milestone planned, completed, blocked, deed signed and disbursed events consumed by the contract vault, commission reconciliation, production dashboards, the customer 360 profile and analytics.

governance.retention: kept 10 years with the credit file; notary and bank contact details pruned to the deed reference once the loan is in the vault; follow-up tasks deleted 12 months after completion
governance.sharingPolicy: shared step by step with the bank, insurer or notary responsible for that step only; the household sees the full timeline; never shared with partners not involved in the closing

assets.name: Refinancing Case
assets.description: A case for an existing mortgage holder: the trigger (rate movement, proposal received elsewhere, renovation obligation for a low-EPC home, second home, new build, financing as a self-employed person), the current loan (bank, outstanding balance, rate, remaining term, reinvestment fee, linked insurance), the new financing need, the break-even calculation with notary and file costs, the proposals computed across the 25 banks or with the current bank, the recommendation, the household's decision and the resulting credit file or the reason the case was closed without a loan. Managed by Refinancing and Renovation Loan Cases (refn) alongside the proposal engine.
assets.businessMeaning: The savings-per-case number for refinancers depends on this record: it shows whether beating the current bank was worth the notary fees and who advised what.
assets.accessScope: the household for its own case; the advising expert and office; compliance for sampling; the mortgage workbench team for calculation diagnostics on pseudonymised data; the current bank never sees the case unless the household asks it to counter-offer

interfaces.name: refinancing-case api
interfaces.description: Case creation from an alert, upload or appointment, current-loan capture, break-even computation, proposal comparison, decision recording and credit-file hand-over API used by the expert workbench, monitoring, upload intake and production dashboards.

interfaces.name: refinancing case events
interfaces.description: Case opened, break-even computed, proposal shared, decided, converted to credit file and closed without loan events consumed by savings alerts, production dashboards, the customer 360 profile and analytics.

governance.retention: kept 10 years when the case becomes a loan, as part of the advice record; 5 years when it is closed without a loan, so a household returning after the next rate move is not assessed from scratch; break-even calculations kept as versions
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Peasy and the assigned office; sent to a bank only as a credit file the household approved; a counter-offer request to the current bank only with explicit mandate

rootGroups.name: Insurance, Energy and Telecom Brokerage Data
rootGroups.description: Quotes, bound policies, switch orders and cancellations executed by the Hasselt and Oujda care centres, and the tickets and knowledge base behind every contact.

subGroups.name: Quotes, Policies, Switches and Cancellations
subGroups.description: Insurance quotes and policies across 11 insurers, energy and telecom switch orders and the termination of the old contracts.

assets.name: Insurance Quote
assets.description: A quote for one household from one of the 11 insurers on Verzekeringen.be: product and cover options (car, fire and contents, funeral, outstanding-balance linked to a loan, other covers), risk inputs (vehicle, driver history and claims, dwelling and contents value, insured capital and term, health questions and medical acceptance status for outstanding-balance cover), premium and payment frequency, exclusions and franchises, quote validity, the advisor who prepared it, the advice-record reference, the household's acceptance and the resulting policy. Produced in Insurance Quote and Policy Binding (iqte) from a comparison request, a closing milestone or a savings alert.
assets.businessMeaning: The insurance attach and switch moment: a quote accepted by the household becomes a bound policy, a referral fee and a contract Peasy will monitor.
assets.accessScope: the household for its own quotes; the preparing care advisor or expert; compliance for sampling; the insurer for quotes on its own products; health answers readable only inside the quote and passed to the insurer's medical acceptance, masked everywhere else

interfaces.name: insurance-quote api
interfaces.description: Quote request per insurer, risk-input capture, premium retrieval, medical-acceptance status, validity, acceptance and bind hand-over API used by the care desk, the expert workbench for loan-linked cover, the consumer sites, closing tracking and monitoring.

interfaces.name: insurance quote events
interfaces.description: Quote requested, received, shared, medical acceptance pending or completed, accepted, expired and bound events consumed by policy contracts, closing milestones, commission reconciliation, partner reporting and analytics.

governance.retention: accepted quotes kept 10 years with the policy and advice record; declined or expired quotes kept 2 years for the next comparison, with health answers deleted 30 days after expiry unless the household asks Peasy to keep them; medical acceptance decisions stored only as a status
governance.sharingPolicy: exchanged with the quoting insurer only; health data passed to that insurer alone and never to the warehouse or other partners; competing quotes never disclosed to another insurer; disclosed to the FSMA on request

assets.name: Policy Contract
assets.description: An insurance policy concluded through Peasy: insurer, policy number, product and cover, insured persons, vehicle or dwelling, premium and payment schedule, start date and renewal date, the quote and advice record it came from, the mandate Peasy holds for the household, the commission scheme reference, policy documents and general conditions, endorsements (vehicle change, address change, cover change), the cancellation of the previous contract and status (active, suspended, cancelled, replaced). Bound in Insurance Quote and Policy Binding (iqte), attached to the credit file by closing tracking and mirrored into the household contract vault.
assets.businessMeaning: The concluded contract the insurer pays a referral fee for and the one Peasy promises to keep optimising: every policy is a monitored contract and a future re-comparison.
assets.accessScope: the household for its own policies; care advisors and the assigned expert for households they serve; partner management for commission reconciliation; the insurer sees its own policies; never visible to other insurers or offices

interfaces.name: policy-contract api
interfaces.description: Policy registration from a bound quote, document attachment, endorsement, renewal-date and status API used by the care desk, closing tracking, the contract vault, cancellation handling, commission reconciliation and monitoring.

interfaces.name: policy contract events
interfaces.description: Policy bound, documents received, endorsed, renewed, cancelled and replaced events consumed by the contract vault, cancellation requests, commission reconciliation, savings alerts, partner reporting and analytics.

interfaces.name: policy documents
interfaces.description: Policy schedule, general conditions and endorsements as issued by the insurer, archived per household in the document store.

governance.retention: kept while the policy is active and 10 years after it ends, covering IDD and FSMA intermediation record-keeping and the tax retention of the commission it generated; endorsements kept as versions; deleted on erasure request only when no retention obligation remains
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the issuing insurer as the contracting party; policy references shared with the bank only for loan-linked cover; commission data shared with partner management; never shared with other insurers or used for marketing without consent

assets.name: Switch Order
assets.description: An order to move a household to a new energy supplier or telecom operator: the selected partner product and tariff version, the household and delivery address, EAN meter numbers, meter type and digital-meter status, solar panels and annual consumption for electricity and gas, or current operator, pack, numbers to port and installation needs for internet, TV and mobile, the Easy Switch identifier where the new fixed operator terminates the old contract, requested start date, the mandate and consent references, transmission to the partner and its acknowledgement, activation confirmation, rejections and the advisor handling it. Executed by Energy and Telecom Switch Execution (swch) through the Integration Gateway (intg).
assets.businessMeaning: The switch that Aanbieders.be promises to do for free: an error-free order activated on the requested date is the metric care advisors are measured on and the trigger for the partner's referral fee.
assets.accessScope: the household for its own orders; the executing care advisor and team leads; the platform and integration team for transport diagnostics without personal payload; the receiving partner for its own orders; EAN numbers masked in analytics

interfaces.name: switch-order api
interfaces.description: Order creation from a selected comparison option, EAN and porting-data capture, mandate check, partner transmission, acknowledgement and activation tracking, rejection handling and vault hand-over API used by the care desk, the consumer sites, the integration gateway, monitoring and cancellation handling.

interfaces.name: switch order events
interfaces.description: Order created, transmitted, acknowledged, rejected, activated and cancelled events consumed by the contract vault, cancellation requests, commission reconciliation, partner reporting, care-centre dashboards and analytics.

interfaces.name: partner switch message
interfaces.description: The order file or API payload as sent to the supplier or operator and its confirmation, kept as transmitted for disputes.

governance.retention: kept 10 years after activation because the order underpins the contract in the vault and the commission Peasy invoiced; rejected or cancelled orders kept 3 years; EAN numbers and consumption pruned to the contract record once activated
governance.sharingPolicy: transmitted to the chosen supplier or operator only; the losing supplier informed only through the regulated switching or Easy Switch process; never shared with other partners; disclosed to the regulator on request

assets.name: Cancellation Request
assets.description: The termination of a household's old contract that Peasy handles as part of a switch or on request: contract type and current insurer, supplier or operator, policy or customer number, notice period and the earliest termination date computed from the contract rules, the mandate signed by the household, the cancellation letter or electronic notice generated in NL or FR, the channel (registered mail, e-mail, partner portal, Easy Switch by the new operator), proof of dispatch and receipt, the partner's confirmation or objection, and the link to the new policy or switch order. Handled by Cancellation and Old-Contract Termination (cncl).
assets.businessMeaning: The paperwork the household never wants to do: a cancellation sent on the right date with proof is what prevents double premiums and the complaints that follow them.
assets.accessScope: the household for its own requests and proofs; the handling care advisor and team leads; compliance for complaint handling; the old partner receives the notice only; never visible to the new partner beyond the effective date

interfaces.name: cancellation api
interfaces.description: Notice-period and termination-date computation, mandate check, letter generation, dispatch and proof recording, confirmation and objection handling API used by the care desk, policy binding, switch execution and the customer account.

interfaces.name: cancellation events
interfaces.description: Cancellation prepared, mandate signed, sent, confirmed, objected and effective events consumed by the contract vault, policy contracts, switch orders, care-centre dashboards and analytics.

interfaces.name: cancellation letter
interfaces.description: The generated notice and the proof of dispatch and receipt, archived per household in the document store.

governance.retention: kept 10 years with the policy or switch it belongs to, because proof of a timely cancellation is what settles a double-premium dispute; stand-alone cancellation requests kept 5 years
governance.sharingPolicy: sent to the old insurer, supplier or operator as the household's mandated notice; never shared with the new partner beyond the effective date; disclosed to an ombudsman on request

subGroups.name: Customer Care
subGroups.description: Omnichannel care tickets and the scripts and knowledge articles advisors work from.

assets.name: Care Ticket
assets.description: One customer-care interaction handled in Hasselt or Oujda: channel (phone, chat, e-mail, callback, customer account), the household and contract concerned, category (comparison, quote, switch, cancellation, monitoring alert, complaint intake, document question, appointment change), the advisor and queue, the script and knowledge articles used, actions taken (comparison run, quote sent, switch ordered, cancellation prepared, expert booked), first-contact resolution flag, follow-up tasks and due dates, the call recording reference, customer satisfaction response and closure. Managed in Customer-Care Ticketing and Omnichannel Inbox (tckt).
assets.businessMeaning: The unit of first-contact resolution: a ticket closed in one contact with an error-free switch is the care centres' north star and the raw material of the customer 360 profile.
assets.accessScope: the handling advisor and queue; care-centre team leads in Hasselt and Oujda; the assigned expert for households of their office; compliance for complaint escalation; the household sees its own requests; call recordings only for quality review and disputes

interfaces.name: care-ticket api
interfaces.description: Ticket creation from any channel, household and contract linking, categorisation, script and knowledge lookup, action logging, follow-up tasks, resolution flag and satisfaction capture API used by the care desk, the customer account, monitoring, the expert workbench and compliance.

interfaces.name: care ticket events
interfaces.description: Ticket opened, assigned, action taken, escalated to an expert or to compliance, resolved, reopened and closed events consumed by the customer 360 profile, savings alerts, complaint records, care-centre dashboards and analytics.

governance.retention: tickets kept 3 years after closure for service quality and repeat-contact detection; tickets that became a complaint or a contract kept with that record for 10 years; call recordings deleted after 90 days unless attached to a complaint or dispute
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Peasy care centres and the assigned office; Oujda advisors work through controlled remote sessions on EU-hosted systems with no local storage; ticket content never shared with partners beyond the action it triggered

assets.name: Knowledge Article
assets.description: An internal article for advisors and experts: call and chat scripts per category, product and partner fact sheets (cover options, tariff peculiarities, digital meter and prosumer rules, Easy Switch steps, notary and renovation obligation explanations), objection handling, compliance do's and don'ts for advice and consent, process guides for quotes, switches and cancellations, escalation rules, and the academy's reference material; with owner, review date, language, applicable brands and partners and an approval trail. Maintained in the Advisor Knowledge Base and Scripts (know) by the care centres with input from compliance and the academy.
assets.businessMeaning: What lets a career changer in Oujda or Hasselt give the same answer as a ten-year expert in Zaventem: consistent scripts and product facts are the cheapest quality lever the care centres have.
assets.accessScope: all advisors, experts and academy trainees read; care-centre team leads and the academy author; compliance approves articles about advice, consent and regulated claims; partners may review fact sheets about their own products; no household data inside

interfaces.name: knowledge api
interfaces.description: Article search and retrieval by category, brand and partner, script rendering inside the care desk, review-workflow and approval API used by the care desk, the expert workbench, the academy and the content pages.

interfaces.name: knowledge events
interfaces.description: Article drafted, approved, published, reviewed and retired events consumed by the care desk, the academy and analytics.

governance.retention: published versions kept 5 years so the guidance an advisor followed at any date can be shown in a complaint review; drafts deleted 12 months after abandonment
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Peasy; partner fact sheets shared with the partner concerned for accuracy review; never published to households

rootGroups.name: Network and Partner Operations Data
rootGroups.description: The office network, its experts and academy, and the partner agreements, commission statements and payouts that carry the referral-fee business model of more than 50 partners and about 70 offices.

subGroups.name: Offices, Experts and Academy
subGroups.description: Office and franchise profiles, expert profiles and registrations, production metrics and the learning records of the Peasy academy.

assets.name: Office Profile
assets.description: One of the about 70 hypotheek.winkel offices or a Meilleurtaux office joining the combined network: address, opening hours, languages, the franchisee entity and franchise agreement reference, the FSMA registration of the office as credit and insurance intermediary, the experts working there and their capacity, the postcodes and municipalities it serves for lead routing, video-call availability, Google review link and rating snapshot, local marketing settings, commission split rules with the network and status (opening, active, transferring, closed). Mastered in Office and Franchise Management (offc) and shown on the office locator.
assets.businessMeaning: The node of the phygital network: routing, capacity, production and payout all key on the office, and the office page is where a buyer decides which expert to trust.
assets.accessScope: network development and franchise for the full profile; the franchisee for their own office; lead routing and appointment booking read capacity and coverage; partner management reads commission split rules; the public sees address, hours, experts and reviews on the locator

interfaces.name: office-profile api
interfaces.description: Office lookup by postcode and municipality, capacity and coverage, expert roster, franchise and registration attributes, commission split rules and public locator data API used by lead routing, appointment booking, the office locator, production dashboards and commission payout.

interfaces.name: office events
interfaces.description: Office opened, franchisee changed, expert joined or left, coverage changed, capacity changed and office closed events consumed by lead routing, appointment booking, production dashboards, commission payout and analytics.

governance.retention: kept for the life of the office and 10 years after closure because payouts and advice records refer to it; franchise agreement references kept per the agreement; public locator data removed on closure
governance.sharingPolicy: public locator data shared on the brand sites; franchise and commission terms confidential between Peasy and the franchisee; FSMA registration data confirmed with the regulator's public register; Meilleurtaux offices governed by the group's integration agreement

assets.name: Expert Profile
assets.description: A hypotheek.expert or insurance advisor in the network: name and contact details, office and employment or franchise relationship, FSMA registration status and number as credit and insurance intermediary or as a person in contact with the public, academy certifications and continuing-education hours, languages, specialities (self-employed borrowers, new build, refinancing, insurance), capacity and calendar settings, review ratings, production targets, commission split and status (in training, certified, active, suspended, left). Mastered in Office and Franchise Management (offc) and updated by the academy and compliance.
assets.businessMeaning: The scarce resource the whole model depends on: about 150 experts largely trained in-house, whose registration and certification determine who is allowed to advise a household at all.
assets.accessScope: the expert for their own profile; the franchisee for experts of their office; network development, the academy and compliance for registration, certification and suspension; lead routing and appointment booking read specialities and capacity; households see name, office and specialities

interfaces.name: expert-profile api
interfaces.description: Expert lookup, registration and certification status, speciality and capacity, office assignment, target and commission split API used by lead routing, appointment booking, the expert workbench, the academy, franchise management and compliance.

interfaces.name: expert events
interfaces.description: Expert recruited, enrolled, certified, registered with the FSMA, assigned to an office, suspended and left events consumed by identity scopes, lead routing, production dashboards, the academy and the audit trail.

governance.retention: kept for the duration of the engagement and 10 years after departure because advice records must remain attributable to a registered person; certification evidence kept as long as the FSMA requires; contact details and ratings pruned 2 years after departure
governance.sharingPolicy: registration status confirmed against the FSMA public register; name, office and specialities shown to households; targets and commission splits confidential between Peasy, the franchisee and the expert; never shared with partners

assets.name: Production Metric
assets.description: The monthly and daily figures per office, expert and brand computed for franchisees and head office: leads received and response time, appointments and attendance, feasibility certificates issued, files opened, first-time-complete rate, banks compared per file, submissions, approvals and turnaround, deeds and loan volume, insurance attach rate, policies, switches and cancellations, commissions earned and paid, conversion rates along the funnel, and comparison with the network average. Computed by Production and Conversion Dashboards (prod) from the aggregated events of the Analytics and Data Platform (anly) and the lead funnel, and read back by analytics, commissions and the academy.
assets.businessMeaning: The scoreboard franchisees run their business on and the basis of every payout discussion: one shared set of numbers keeps 70 offices and head office arguing about tactics, not data.
assets.accessScope: franchisees and experts for their own office and personal figures; network development and head-office management for the whole network; partner management for commission-linked figures; never shown to households or partners at office level

interfaces.name: production-metric api
interfaces.description: Funnel, production, conversion and commission figures per office, expert, brand and period with network benchmarks API used by the production dashboards, franchise management, commission payout and the academy.

interfaces.name: production metric events
interfaces.description: Period closed, metric recomputed and target breached events consumed by franchise management, commission payout, network development alerts and analytics.

governance.retention: monthly aggregates kept 10 years for franchise and payout history; daily figures kept 3 years; expert-level figures pruned to office level 2 years after an expert leaves
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with each franchisee for their own offices and with head office for the network; partners receive only aggregated figures about their own products; never shared between franchisees except as anonymised benchmarks

assets.name: Academy Enrolment
