assets.description: The learning record of one person in the Peasy academy: the trainee (career changer, new expert, care advisor, existing expert on continuing education), sponsoring office or care centre, programme (mortgage credit intermediation, insurance distribution, energy and telecom advice, workbench and care-desk tooling), module completions and exam results, practical hours in an office, FSMA professional-knowledge evidence and the registration application it supports, certification date, continuing-education hours per year, trainer feedback and status. Managed in Academy Learning and Certification (acad) for about 30 advisors trained per year.
assets.businessMeaning: How Peasy turns advisor supply into planned capacity: the enrolment record is the evidence that a scarce-skill role was grown in-house to the FSMA standard.
assets.accessScope: the trainee for their own record; academy trainers and the academy team; the sponsoring franchisee or care-centre lead for progress; compliance for registration evidence; never shared with households or partners

interfaces.name: academy-enrolment api
interfaces.description: Enrolment, module and exam progress, practical-hour logging, certification and continuing-education status API used by the academy, franchise management, expert profiles, the knowledge base and compliance.

interfaces.name: academy events
interfaces.description: Trainee enrolled, module completed, exam passed or failed, certified, continuing-education due and programme abandoned events consumed by expert profiles, identity scopes, production dashboards and analytics.

governance.retention: kept for the duration of the person's engagement and 10 years after departure as evidence of professional knowledge for FSMA registrations; exam papers deleted 2 years after the exam; abandoned enrolments deleted after 3 years
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Peasy, the academy and the sponsoring office; certification evidence disclosed to the FSMA for registration; never shared with partners

subGroups.name: Partners and Commissions
subGroups.description: Partner agreements with fee schedules, reconciled commission statements and the payouts to the office network.

assets.name: Partner Agreement
assets.description: The commercial relationship with one of the more than 50 partners paying referral fees: the bank, insurer, energy supplier or telecom operator entity and contacts, agreement term and notice, the products in scope of the comparison modules or the bank comparison, referral fee (aanbrengvergoeding) schedules per product and volume tier, bonus and clawback rules, data-exchange and tariff-feed obligations, service levels for file approval or switch activation, reconciliation frequency, the partner portal users and status (negotiating, active, suspended, ended). Mastered in Partner Product Catalogue and Tariff Feeds (pcat) with the Partner Portal and Lead Exchange (pprt).
assets.businessMeaning: The contract behind the free-for-consumers model: the agreement decides what Peasy earns per concluded contract and what it owes the partner in data and volume.
assets.accessScope: partner management and head-office management; compliance for the independence and disclosure clauses; commission reconciliation reads fee schedules; the partner sees its own agreement in the portal; fee schedules never visible to experts, franchisees or households

interfaces.name: partner-agreement api
interfaces.description: Agreement lookup, product scope, fee schedule and clawback rules, service levels, portal user management and status API used by the partner catalogue, commission reconciliation, the partner portal, the bank rate feed and compliance.

interfaces.name: partner agreement events
interfaces.description: Agreement signed, product added or removed, fee schedule changed, service-level breached, suspended and ended events consumed by the tariff store, commission reconciliation, the partner portal and analytics.

interfaces.name: signed agreement
interfaces.description: The signed contract, annexes and fee schedules as PDF, archived in the document store.

governance.retention: kept for the term of the agreement and 10 years after it ends, covering tax retention of the fees it generated and FSMA disclosure obligations; portal user data deleted 2 years after the user is removed
governance.sharingPolicy: confidential between Peasy and the partner; fee levels disclosed to households only in the generic form the FSMA requires (that partners pay a fee per concluded contract); never shared with other partners or franchisees

assets.name: Commission Statement
assets.description: A periodic statement of referral fees from one partner, reconciled against Peasy's own records: the period and partner, statement lines per concluded contract (bank loan by deed reference, policy by policy number, energy or telecom switch by order reference), fee amount, bonus tier and clawbacks for early termination, the matching Peasy record and the attribution to office, expert or care advisor, discrepancies (missing contracts, wrong amounts, unrecognised references), dispute status with the partner, and the approved total that flows into the network payout. Produced by Commission Reconciliation and Network Payout (comm) from policies, switch orders and bank submissions.
assets.businessMeaning: Where the revenue of about €30 million is actually confirmed: a reconciled statement is the difference between the referral fee Peasy earned and the one it got paid.
assets.accessScope: partner management and finance; the partner for its own statements through the portal; franchisees and experts see only the attribution lines for their own office after approval; compliance for disclosure checks; contract references pseudonymised in the warehouse

interfaces.name: commission-statement api
interfaces.description: Statement import per partner, line matching against contracts, discrepancy and dispute handling, attribution to office and advisor, approval and payout hand-over API used by commission reconciliation, the partner portal, production dashboards and network payout.

interfaces.name: commission statement events
interfaces.description: Statement received, matched, discrepancy raised, disputed, resolved and approved events consumed by network payout, partner reporting, production dashboards and analytics.

interfaces.name: partner statement
interfaces.description: The statement file as received from the bank, insurer, supplier or operator and the reconciliation report returned to it.

governance.retention: kept 10 years as accounting and tax records of Peasy's revenue; dispute correspondence kept with the statement; contract references pruned to the statement line once the payout is settled
governance.sharingPolicy: exchanged with the issuing partner only; office and advisor attribution shared with the franchisee concerned; never shared between partners; disclosed to auditors and tax authorities as required

assets.name: Network Payout
assets.description: The periodic settlement of commission shares to the office network: per franchisee entity and per expert or care advisor, the approved commission lines from reconciled statements, the split rules from the office profile and franchise agreement, franchise fees and marketing contributions netted, clawbacks applied, adjustments and corrections, the resulting payout amount, self-billing or invoice reference, bank details, payment status and the statement delivered to the franchisee with the detail per contract. Produced by Commission Reconciliation and Network Payout (comm) and delivered through the franchise back office.
assets.businessMeaning: The moment the franchise model pays out: a correct, explainable payout to about 70 offices is what keeps franchisees and experts in the network.
assets.accessScope: partner management and finance; the franchisee for their own payout and detail; experts for their own share; network development for disputes; bank details readable only by the payment step; never shared with partners

interfaces.name: network-payout api
interfaces.description: Payout computation from approved commission lines and split rules, netting and clawback application, correction handling, self-billing document generation and payment-status API used by commission reconciliation, franchise management, production dashboards and finance.

interfaces.name: network payout events
interfaces.description: Payout computed, corrected, approved, paid and disputed events consumed by franchise management, production dashboards and analytics.

interfaces.name: payout statement
interfaces.description: The payout statement and self-billing document delivered to each franchisee, archived in the document store.

governance.retention: kept 10 years as accounting and tax records; bank details kept while the payee is active and deleted 2 years after departure; per-contract detail pruned to totals after the retention of the underlying commission statement
governance.sharingPolicy: shared with the franchisee and expert concerned; never shared with partners or between franchisees; disclosed to auditors and tax authorities as required

rootGroups.name: Compliance, Audit and Analytics Data
rootGroups.description: The complaints, audit trail and pseudonymised analytics events that prove FSMA and GDPR compliance across three brands and measure the funnel end to end.

subGroups.name: Complaints, Audit and Analytics
subGroups.description: Complaint records, the immutable audit trail and consent-aware analytics events.

assets.name: Complaint Record
assets.description: A complaint or dispute from a household, partner or regulator about any Peasy brand: the complainant, the contract, file, advice or switch it concerns, the category (advice quality, delay, wrong switch, double premium, data protection, fee disclosure, advisor conduct), intake channel and date, the responsible office or care centre, investigation notes and the evidence gathered from the advice record, tickets and audit trail, the remedy offered, escalation to the Ombudsfin or Ombudsman for Insurance, FSMA or Data Protection Authority correspondence, deadlines, root cause and closure. Managed in Compliance, Complaints and Audit Trail (cmpl).
assets.businessMeaning: The early-warning system of a regulated intermediary: complaint handling within deadlines, with evidence, is what keeps compliance audit findings low and the FSMA registration safe.
assets.accessScope: compliance and risk for the full record; the responsible office or care-centre lead for their own cases; management for escalations; the complainant sees the status and outcome of their own complaint; never visible to other offices, partners or experts not involved

interfaces.name: complaint api
interfaces.description: Complaint intake, linking to contracts, files and tickets, investigation notes, evidence gathering, remedy and escalation, deadline tracking and closure API used by compliance, the care desk, the expert workbench, the customer account and management reporting.

interfaces.name: complaint events
interfaces.description: Complaint received, assigned, escalated to an ombudsman or regulator, remedy offered, closed and reopened events consumed by care tickets, the customer 360 profile, compliance dashboards and analytics.

governance.retention: kept 10 years after closure, aligned with the retention of the advice records and contracts it concerns, and longer while regulatory proceedings run; complainant contact details pruned 2 years after closure when the case did not concern an active contract
governance.sharingPolicy: disclosed to the ombudsman, FSMA, Economic Inspectorate or Data Protection Authority handling the case; shared with the partner only for the contract concerned; never shared between offices or used for marketing

assets.name: Audit Trail Entry
assets.description: An immutable record of one auditable action across the platform: who (user identity, role, office or care centre, remote-session flag for Oujda), what (read of a credit file, export, advice record signed, consent changed, credit register consulted, bank submission released, switch order sent, tariff version published, commission approved, payout paid, configuration changed), on which object, when, from where and through which module, with the before and after values where relevant and the retention tier of the entry. Written by the Integration Gateway (intg) and every module through Compliance, Complaints and Audit Trail (cmpl).
assets.businessMeaning: The evidence layer under three regulated brands: it shows the FSMA who advised, the Data Protection Authority who looked, and a partner what was sent and when.
assets.accessScope: compliance and risk and the platform team for investigations; a household for a report of who accessed its own data on request; franchisees for actions in their own office on request; append-only, no edit or delete rights for anyone

interfaces.name: audit-trail api
interfaces.description: Append-only write from every module and the integration gateway, query by object, user, office, period and action type, and access-report generation API used by compliance, security monitoring, complaint handling and data-subject request handling.

interfaces.name: audit trail events
interfaces.description: Privileged action recorded, suspicious pattern detected and retention tier expired events consumed by security monitoring, compliance dashboards and analytics.

governance.retention: entries about advice, submissions, consents, switches and commissions kept 10 years in line with the records they prove; read and sign-in entries kept 2 years; remote-session entries from Oujda kept 5 years; entries never deleted individually, only by tier expiry
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Peasy; extracts disclosed to the FSMA, the Data Protection Authority, an ombudsman or an auditor on request; a partner receives only the entries about its own exchanges; never shared with franchisees beyond their own office

assets.name: Analytics Event
assets.description: A pseudonymised behavioural event from the brand sites, the customer account, the expert workbench and the care desk: page and simulator views, comparison starts and completions, calculator inputs in banded form, certificate and appointment conversions, upload starts, alert opens, workbench and care-desk actions with duration, campaign and channel attribution, device and language, session and pseudonymous visitor identifiers, consent state at capture, and the experiment variant shown. Collected by the Analytics and Data Platform (anly) with consent handled by the site shell, and joined to production metrics only in aggregate.
assets.businessMeaning: The measurement of the phygital funnel from a Google click to a signed deed: it tells three brands which page, tool and advisor step actually converts.
assets.accessScope: the platform and integration team and product teams for funnel and feature analysis; marketing for attribution in aggregate; compliance for consent audits; never joined to a named household outside the consented account context; never shared with partners at event level

interfaces.name: analytics-event api
interfaces.description: Event ingestion with consent check, pseudonymisation, funnel and cohort queries, experiment assignment and attribution reporting API used by the site shell, the customer account, the workbench, the care desk, production dashboards and monitoring.

interfaces.name: analytics events
interfaces.description: Event batch ingested, funnel threshold crossed, experiment concluded and consent state changed events consumed by dashboards, campaign tools and monitoring rules.

governance.retention: raw events kept 13 months and then aggregated; pseudonymous identifiers rotated every 13 months; events captured without analytics consent limited to strictly necessary measurements and kept 30 days; aggregates kept indefinitely
governance.sharingPolicy: internal to Peasy; aggregated funnel statistics shared with partners and franchisees about their own products or offices; event-level data never sold or shared; processors bound by data-processing agreements with EU hosting

stores.name: Customer CRM DB
stores.description: Relational schema (PostgreSQL-style, one household key across the three brands) for customer accounts, leads, appointments, callback requests, the household contract vault, savings alerts and the customer 360 profile; national register numbers stored in encrypted columns readable only by the mortgage workbench and insurance binding modules, with row-level scoping so an office or care advisor sees only assigned households.

stores.name: Identity Provider DB
stores.description: Identity and access schema behind the single sign-on for households, experts, franchisees, care advisors, partner users and head-office staff: credential hashes, itsme and two-factor assertions, roles and office or brand scopes, sessions, device registrations and the consent registry with effective-dated purposes; kept separate from customer data so authentication can be hardened, rotated and audited independently.

stores.name: Audit Log Store
stores.description: Write-once, hash-chained log of every privileged read, change, export, advice-record release, bank submission, switch order, e-signature event, consent change and remote-access session from the Oujda care centre across all brands, with retention tiers per entry type; the source for GDPR access reports, FSMA inspections and complaint reconstruction.

stores.name: Comparison Engine Tariff Store
stores.description: Versioned tariff and product-rule store behind the Peasy comparison engine: daily rate sheets and conditions of the 25 banks, tariff feeds and product attributes of more than 50 insurance, energy and telecom partners, simulator parameters, comparison requests and results, and budget profiles; every tariff version is effective-dated so any comparison shown to a household can be replayed years later.

stores.name: Mortgage Workbench DB
stores.description: Relational schema of the hypotheek.winkel expert workbench: buyer situation and project, multi-bank proposals and recommendations, advice and suitability records, credit files with document checklists, bank submissions and approval state, closing milestones through compromis and notary deed, and refinancing and renovation cases; scoped per office so an expert reads only their own files, with head-office compliance roles for review.

stores.name: Brokerage Document Store
stores.description: Encrypted object storage organised per household and file for credit-file documents (payslips, tax assessments, savings statements, compromis, EPC certificates, identity copies), uploaded proposals from other banks or brokers, feasibility certificate and comparison PDFs, signed advice records, policy documents, switch confirmations and commission statement PDFs; versioned and immutable once a file is submitted, with retention labels driving deletion.

stores.name: Contact Centre Platform
stores.description: Omnichannel contact-centre platform used in Hasselt and Oujda: telephony, chat, e-mail and callback queues, care tickets, insurance quotes and policy binding state, switch orders and cancellation requests in flight, advisor scripts and the knowledge base; call recordings kept separately with shorter retention, and Oujda access routed through controlled remote sessions to EU-hosted systems.

stores.name: Network and Commission DB
stores.description: Back-office schema for the office network and partner economics: office and franchise profiles, expert profiles and FSMA registrations, partner agreements and fee schedules, monthly production metrics, commission statements received from banks, insurers, energy suppliers and telecom operators, reconciliation results and payouts to about 70 offices and their advisors; the ledger side of the referral-fee business model.

stores.name: Academy LMS
stores.description: Learning-management system of the Peasy academy: enrolments of career changers and new advisors, curriculum modules for mortgage credit and insurance distribution, exam results, FSMA knowledge and professional-competence evidence, certification status and continuing-education hours; holds no household data, only the learning record of about 30 advisors trained per year and the existing network.

stores.name: Operations Analytics Warehouse
stores.description: Analytical warehouse with marts for the funnel from simulation to lead, appointment, file, approval and deed, comparison and switch volumes per partner, contract monitoring and alert acceptance, office production and conversion, care-centre resolution and commission reconciliation, plus a pseudonymised web and app event layer; feeds dashboards and KPI pyramids and is never the source of a household-facing figure.
